about.title: Indian Wells Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Indian Wells draws visitors to its resorts, golf clubs, and shopping areas along corridors like Highway 111 and Washington Street, and property owners there carry a duty to keep walkways, parking areas, and common spaces reasonably safe. When they don't, guests and residents can end up hurt because of a wet pool deck, uneven pavement, poor lighting, or a spill left unaddressed in a store or condo lobby. California law generally requires showing the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn people. That's why documenting the scene, getting witness names, and pushing to preserve any surveillance footage matters early on. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured people in Indian Wells with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost and no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California generally requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or incident reports to establish this.

items.title: Acting Within the Deadline
items.desc: Most premises liability claims must be filed within two years, though claims against a public entity involve much shorter windows. Waiting too long can close off your options entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Considerations
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning a partial share of blame doesn't necessarily bar recovery, but it can reduce it. An independent attorney can help address how fault gets allocated in your specific fall.

items.question: I fell at a resort in Indian Wells but wasn't sure who to report it to. Does that hurt my claim?
items.answer: Not reporting it right away can make things harder, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. What matters most is documenting the hazard as soon as possible: photos, witness names, and any incident report you can still request. An attorney can help track down surveillance footage from the property before it's deleted.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, though claims against a government-owned property have much shorter deadlines, sometimes just months. It's worth having a claim reviewed sooner rather than later so nothing gets missed.

items.question: Will I still recover something if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovery, though it may reduce what you're able to claim. Every situation is different, and an independent attorney can walk through the specifics of your fall.
